findings.rationale: Subgroup screen at Sex=1.0 shows MT's observed/expected ratio far below the federation median (0.345 vs median 1.126; z_noise -5.6), i.e. positives in this subgroup are recorded as negative. Its local CITL is positive (mean predicted above observed, citl z=+3.3), and its updates are anomalous: norm ratio rises steadily from 1.16 (round 1) to 2.34 (round 20), and cosine to the median falls from about 0.85 in round 1 to -1 in round 20. The cosine drops below about 0.4 at round 6 and goes negative from round 10-11, so the onset is estimated at round 6. The per-round data for MT is from the client_updates call, not a subgroup-by-round table, so the onset is approximate.

Subgroup screen at Sex=1.0 shows MD's observed/expected ratio at about half the federation median (0.483 vs median 1.126; z_noise -4.8). Its updates are anomalous across the run: the mean cosine to the median update is negative (-0.058, mean_cos z=-4.3) and the median norm ratio is 3.07 (z=+3.8). MD's local AUC and ECE look normal, which argues against label noise or poisoning. Onset is estimated at round 1 because the anomaly summaries cover all 20 rounds, but there is no per-round breakdown for MD, so this is a lower-confidence onset.

Subgroup screen at Sex=1.0 shows WA's observed/expected ratio well below the federation median (0.461 vs median 1.126; z_noise -5.0). WA's updates are the most extreme in the federation (median norm ratio 4.21, z=+3.9; min cosine -0.80, z=-3.9), and its mean cosine is near zero (0.045, z=-3.6). Its local AUC is normal (0.814) and its CITL is modestly positive (0.034, not flagged). Onset is estimated at round 1 from the run-wide anomaly summaries; there is no per-round breakdown for WA, so this onset is lower confidence.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (MT, MD, WA) show the same under-diagnosis signature: observed/expected ratio in Sex=1.0 is roughly 0.35-0.48 against a federation median of 1.13, with z_noise between -4.8 and -5.6. All three also have anomalous updates (negative or near-zero cosine to the median, norm ratios 2-4x the median). MT's anomaly grows over time, starting around round 6, and its CITL is also flagged. I reported these as subgroup_bias. I did not report poisoning, because their local AUC and ECE look normal and the subgroup evidence explains the update anomalies. Other flags were weak: GU's update-norm and ECE z-scores, GA/WV/NV AgeGroup outliers from small subgroups, and scattered feature-level z-scores from small clients (DC, GU, VI, NV). The AL drift flag from the first screen did not persist in the narrower drift query, so I did not report it. Budget is fully spent (20.0 epsilon used).
